newsitem.title: THAILAND: Politics may delay Thai coffee policy meeting.
newsitem.headline: Politics may delay Thai coffee policy meeting.

text.p: A Thai government meeting on 1996/97 (October-September) coffee policy might be delayed due to the pending change of government following Sunday's general election, a senior commerce ministry official said on Monday.

The meeting, originally scheduled for November 30, is for the government to discuss coffee prices and exports policy, Manas Soiploy, a director of the ministry's agricultural trade division, told Reuters.
There had been talk earlier that the government might seek to guarantee the coffee price for local planters at 30 baht ($1.20) a kg.
Manas said that the possible postponment was also due to a delay in harvesting due to a prolonged rainy season.
"A delay could benefit the meeting and farmers as we will have a clearer picture of output and world market trend," he said.
"We will have to look at world prices, supply and production cost before making any decision on price support policy."
Thailand exported about 60,000 tonnes of coffee beans in 1995 from an estimated output of 78,801 tonnes, according to official figures.
The agriculture ministry has forecast coffee output this year at 81,398 tonnes although private sources projected that it could reach 90,000 tonnes.
Traders expected that about 65,000 tonnes would be exported this year.
